start.title: Who Is My Neighbor?
start.text:
Jesus sits on the hillside.
"Let me tell you a story."

choices.feedback: Luke 10:25-29 — Jesus told the parable of the Good Samaritan in response to a lawyer's question, "Who is my neighbor?"

walk_consequence.title: Turn Back
walk_consequence.text:
Some stories find you anyway.
Return and listen.

rule_consequence.title: Listen First
rule_consequence.text:
Love is not a rule to memorize.
It is a road to walk.

attack.title: Down to Jericho
attack.text:
A man walked the lonely road.
Robbers left him beaten, alone.

choices.feedback: Luke 10:30 — The man was traveling from Jerusalem to Jericho when he was attacked by robbers.

pity_consequence.title: See Him
pity_consequence.text:
Compassion must open its eyes.
Look at him fully.

priest.title: A Priest Passes By
priest.text:
A priest walked the same road.
He saw the man, then crossed over.

choices.feedback: Luke 10:31 — A priest saw the injured man but passed by on the other side of the road.

cheer_consequence.title: Not Yet
cheer_consequence.text:
Holy clothes did not soften him.
Mercy is the holier robe.

excuse_consequence.title: No Excuse
excuse_consequence.text:
Love makes time it does not have.
Feel the wound.

levite.title: A Levite Passes By
levite.text:
Then a Levite came near.
He looked, then walked away too.

choices.feedback: Luke 10:32 — A Levite also came to the place, saw the man, and passed by on the other side.

hope_consequence.title: Be the Neighbor
hope_consequence.text:
The world waits for someone.
Let that someone be you.

samaritan.title: A Samaritan Stops
samaritan.text:
A Samaritan saw the broken man.
He knelt down beside him.

choices.feedback: Luke 10:33 — A Samaritan, as he traveled, came where the man was and took pity on him.

doubt_consequence.title: No Borders
doubt_consequence.text:
He is the neighbor you did not expect.
Receive his goodness.

tend.title: Oil and Wine
tend.text:
He cleansed the wounds with care.
He bound them with his own cloth.

choices.text: Rush him: it takes too long

choices.feedback: Luke 10:34 — The Samaritan bandaged the man's wounds, pouring on oil and wine.

rush_consequence.title: Be Patient
rush_consequence.text:
Healing cannot be hurried.
Stay near him.

lookaway_consequence.title: Stay With Him
lookaway_consequence.text:
Mercy does not turn away.
It stays through the hard part.

inn.title: Bring Him to Shelter
inn.text:
He lifted the man onto his donkey.
He carried him to a quiet inn.

choices.feedback: Luke 10:34 — The Samaritan put the man on his own donkey and took him to an inn.

leave_consequence.title: Finish the Mercy
leave_consequence.text:
Half-finished kindness still wounds.
See him fully settled.

pay.title: Two Silver Coins
pay.text:
"Care for him. I will return
and repay whatever it costs."

choices.feedback: Luke 10:35 — The Samaritan gave the innkeeper two denarii and promised to repay any extra expenses upon his return.

minimum_consequence.title: Go Further
minimum_consequence.text:
Love does not count its coins.
It covers what is needed.

ending.title: Go and Do Likewise
ending.text:
Jesus looks straight at you.
"Go now. Do the same."
